chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Jahm, from Rifa'ah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Girith, so he said, 'By Allah, I have never seen it, but we found it in the book of Ali (peace be upon him) to be Haram (forbidden).'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.الْجِرِيثِ: Girith, a specific type of fish or seafood mentioned in hadith
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali, a primary source of fiqh attributed to Imam Ali

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Girith in Shia jurisprudence according to the book of Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on the 'Girith' by distinguishing between personal observation and transmitted knowledge, citing its prohibition in the 'Book of Imam Ali' (Kitab Ali), which likely refers to the foundational legal traditions or the specific treatise on hunting and slaughter attributed to him. This narration highlights the Shia reliance on the Ahl al-Bayt's compiled legal corpus for determining the status of specific marine creatures not explicitly detailed in the Quran.
